attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this assessment in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both historical assertions and Marcus's subjective qualifier. That qualifier expresses judgment, not probabilistic confidence.

contract.note: Repeated deadline failures and recurring uncritical coverage are fair ordinary readings. The contract appropriately separates the components without requiring every prediction to fail or all coverage to be credulous.

evidence.note: The dated audit supports repeated timeline failures, with acknowledged sampling limitations. It does not establish the media component.
Reuters corroborates repeated missed deadlines. Its critical coverage also limits sweeping interpretations of the media criticism, without disproving recurring credulity.
This contemporaneous article explicitly questions Musk's forecasting. One skeptical article cannot establish or refute the claimed frequency of uncritical coverage.

reviews.rationale: The audit and Reuters reporting support the repeated-deadline-failure component. No defined, sufficiently broad coverage sample establishes or refutes recurring uncritical reporting. The skeptical examples do not disprove that pattern, so the combined claim remains unresolved.
